For American football player with the nickname "Sugar Land Express", see [Ken Hall (American football)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Hall_%28American_football%29).

**The Sugarland Express** is a 1974 American [crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_drama) film directed by [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg).<sup>[3]</sup> The film follows a woman ([Goldie Hawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldie_Hawn)) and her husband ([William Atherton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Atherton)) as they take a police officer ([Michael Sacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Sacks)) hostage and flee across Texas while they try to get to their child before he is placed in foster care. The film was based on true events, some of which occurred in [Sugar Land, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_Land,_Texas), where parts of the film were shot.<sup>[4]</sup> Other scenes were filmed in [San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio,_Texas), [Live Oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Oak,_Texas), [Floresville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floresville,_Texas), [Pleasanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasanton,_Texas), [Converse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converse,_Texas) and [Del Rio, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Del_Rio,_Texas).<sup>[5]</sup>

The Sugarland Express marks the first collaboration between Spielberg and composer [John Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Williams), who has scored all but five of Spielberg's films since. Although Williams rerecorded the main theme with [Toots Thielemans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toots_Thielemans) and the [Boston Pops Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Pops_Orchestra) for 1991's The Spielberg/Williams Collaboration,<sup>[6]</sup> the score was not released as an album until June 15, 2024, coinciding with the film's 50th anniversary.<sup>[7]</sup>

The film premiered at the [New Directors/New Films Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Directors/New_Films_Festival) on March 29, 1974, and was released theatrically in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City) on March 31, 1974, followed by a year-long worldwide theatrical rollout. The film was a commercial disappointment but received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised Hawn's performance, Spielberg's direction, and the cinematography.<sup>[8]</sup> The film has become a [cult classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_classic) as a staple in the new Hollywood era which launched the career of Steven Spielberg.

Early life and family [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nagarjuna_%28actor%29&action=edit&section=1)

Akkineni Nagarjuna was born on 29 August 1959 at St. Isabel's Hospital in [Madras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madras) (present-day Chennai),<sup>[2]</sup> into a [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_people) speaking family of veteran actor [Akkineni Nageswara Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akkineni_Nageswara_Rao) and Annapurna ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%A9e) Kollipara) . He was the youngest of 5 kids. His family hails from [Ramapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramapuram_%28Venkata_Raghava_Puram%29) in [Krishna District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_District) of [Andhra Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh).<sup>[18]</sup>

The family later moved to Hyderabad, where he did his schooling in [Hyderabad Public School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad_Public_School) and [intermediate education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_Grade#India) from [Little Flower Junior College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Flower_Junior_College), [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad). He completed the first year of his [Mechanical Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanical_Engineering) undergraduation at the [College of Engineering, Guindy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Engineering,_Guindy), [Anna University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_University) in Madras,<sup>[19]</sup> where former Indian cricketer [Krishnamachari Srikanth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishnamachari_Srikkanth) was his college mate. He then transferred to [Eastern Michigan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Michigan_University) in [Ypsilanti, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ypsilanti,_Michigan) where he earned a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering.<sup>[20][21]</sup>

1961–1988: Early career and success [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nagarjuna_%28actor%29&action=edit&section=3)

Nagarjuna stepped into the field of acting as an infant in the movie [Velugu Needalu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velugu_Needalu) (1961).<sup>[22]</sup> He began acting as a child artist in [Sudigundalu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudigundalu) (1967) directed by [Adurthi Subba Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adurthi_Subba_Rao). Both movies starred his father [Akkineni Nageswara Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akkineni_Nageswara_Rao) in the lead role.<sup>[23]</sup> Years later he made his debut as a lead actor through the 1986 Telugu film [Vikram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikram_%281986_Telugu_film%29), directed by [V. Madhusudhana Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Madhusudhana_Rao). It is the remake of the 1983 [Hindi film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_film) [Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hero_%281983_film%29). The film was a success, giving Nagarjuna a good start. Later, he starred in films like [Majnu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majnu_%281987_film%29), directed by [Dasari Narayana Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dasari_Narayana_Rao), which was well received. Nagarjuna got positive reviews for his portrayal of a heartbroken man. He then starred in [Sankeertana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sankeertana), a below average grosser directed by debutant [Geetha Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geetha_Krishna) with music by [Ilaiyaraaja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilaiyaraaja). The film was appreciated for its content and music. In 1988, he starred in the blockbuster [Aakhari Poratam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aakhari_Poratam), scripted by [Yandamuri Veerendranath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yandamuri_Veerendranath), and directed by [K. Raghavendra Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Raghavendra_Rao) where he was paired opposite [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi) and [Suhasini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suhasini_Maniratnam). In 1988, he starred in [Janaki Ramudu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janaki_Ramudu) alongside [Vijayashanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayashanti) was directed again by K. Raghavendra Rao.
1989–1999: Breakthrough and Stardom [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nagarjuna_%28actor%29&action=edit&section=4)

In 1989, he starred in the [Mani Ratnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mani_Ratnam)-directed [romantic drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_drama_film) [Geetanjali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geethanjali_%281989_film%29).<sup>[24]</sup> The film won the [National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Popular_Film_Providing_Wholesome_Entertainment) in 1990. Immediately, he saw another success, [Siva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siva_%281989_Telugu_film%29). This film marked the debut of director [Ram Gopal Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Gopal_Varma). **Laura Mennell** ([/mɛˈnɛl/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English); born 18 April 1980) is a Canadian actress known for her roles in [Thirteen Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteen_Ghosts), [Alphas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphas), [Haven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haven_%28TV_series%29), [Loudermilk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudermilk_%28TV_series%29), [The Man in the High Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_%28TV_series%29), [Watchmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watchmen_%282009_film%29) and [Batwoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batwoman_%28TV_series%29). In 2011/2012 Mennell co-starred on the [sci-fi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction) [television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_show) [Alphas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphas). Laura appeared as Charlotte Cross in the fifth season of the [Syfy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syfy) series [Haven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haven_%28TV_series%29), and she starred in the comedy series [Loudermilk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudermilk_%28TV_series%29) from 2017 to 2018.

Early and personal life [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vijayakanth&action=edit&section=1)

Vijayakanth was born as Vijayaraj Alagarswami in [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai) on 25 August 1952.<sup>[2][3][4]</sup> His parents were K. N. Alagarswami and Aandal.<sup>[1]</sup> Vijayakanth grew up idolising [M. G. Ramachandran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._G._Ramachandran) and displayed passion towards community and societal issues.<sup>[5]</sup> During his young age, his father was concerned about Vijayakanth as he showed less interest towards studies and was more interested in cinema.<sup>[6]</sup>  His father ran a [rice mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_mill) at Keeraithurai where Vijayakanth went on to work and surprised him with his administrative skills.<sup>[7]</sup>

Vijayakanth married [Premalatha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premalatha_Vijayakanth) on 31 January 1990 and the couple have two sons– [Shanmuga Pandian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanmuga_Pandian) and Vijaya Prabhakaran.<sup>[8][9]</sup>

In 1978, Vijayakanth engaged in a [photo shoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photo_shoot) in Rasi Studios in Madurai with the aim of acting in films, which helped him garner attention.<sup>[10]</sup>  He later gave credit to the chief photographer R. Asaithambi, indicating that the photographs eventually helped him earn a spot in the film industry. <sup>[11]</sup> Vijayakanth travelled to Chennai to pursue his passion in acting, even though he did not have any cinematic background.<sup>[5]</sup> He was cast in a supporting role as [Rajnikanth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajnikanth)'s younger brother in [En Kelvikku Enna Bathil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/En_Kelvikku_Enna_Bathil) (1978) by the director [P. Madhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._Madhavan), for which he received an advance of ₹100 (equivalent to ₹3,000 or US\$31 in 2026). <sup>[12]</sup> However, he was later replaced by [Ceylon Manohar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceylon_Manohar) after the director was unimpressed with Vijayakanth's acting.<sup>[13][14]</sup> He claimed to have lost several film opportunities during the early stages of his acting career largely due to his darker complexion.<sup>[15][16][17]</sup> In 1979, Vijayakanth made his first film appearance in M. Soundtracks of [The Bodyguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bodyguard_%28soundtrack%29) and [The Preacher's Wife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Preacher's_Wife_%28soundtrack%29), respectively, rank as the best-selling soundtrack album and gospel album of all time, with the former winning the [Grammy Award for Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year) and topping the Billboard 200 for 20 weeks.

Following the success of [My Love Is Your Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Love_Is_Your_Love) (1998), Houston's first studio album in eight years, she renewed her contract with Arista Records for \$100 million in 2001, one of the [largest recording deals of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_music_deals). However, her drug use and a tumultuous marriage to singer [Bobby Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Brown) tarnished her "[America's Sweetheart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Sweetheart#Race)" image, overshadowing her next albums, [Just Whitney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_Whitney) (2002) and [One Wish: The Holiday Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Wish:_The_Holiday_Album) (2003). After divorcing Brown, Houston returned to the top of the Billboard 200 with her final album, [I Look to You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Look_to_You) (2009). On February 11, 2012, [Houston accidentally drowned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Whitney_Houston) in a bathtub at the [Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton) hotel in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California), with heart disease and cocaine use as contributing factors. News of her death coincided with the [54th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards) and [broke Internet and television records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Whitney_Houston#Media_coverage_and_internet_activity). Houston's death was covered internationally along with her [memorial service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_Houston_memorial_service).

Houston's first two albums, along with The Bodyguard soundtrack, rank among the [best-selling albums of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_albums) and made her the first black artist to score three [RIAA diamond-](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification#Artists_with_the_most_album_certifications)

[certified albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification#Artists_with_the_most_album_certifications). "[I Wanna Dance with Somebody (Who Loves Me)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wanna_Dance_with_Somebody_%28Who_Loves_Me%29)" and "[I Will Always Love You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Will_Always_Love_You_%28Whitney_Houston_recording%29)" are among the [best-selling singles ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles); the latter remains the best-selling single by a woman and has been certified [diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-certified_digital_singles_in_the_United_States) by the RIAA. Houston scored [eleven number-one singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artists_with_the_most_number-ones_on_the_U.S._Billboard_Hot_100_chart) on the [Billboard Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100) and remains the only artist to have [seven consecutive singles top the chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_consecutive_number-one_songs). She has been inducted into [multiple halls and walks of fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Whitney_Houston#Cultural_honors), including the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame), the [Rhythm & Blues Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Rhythm_&_Blues_Hall_of_Fame), and the [Grammy Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Hall_of_Fame) (twice). [Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Records) named Houston the [highest-earning posthumous female celebrity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes_list_of_the_world's_highest-paid_dead_celebrities). Her assets amounted to \$250 million, earned over a 25-year career. Her life and career have been the subject of multiple documentaries and television specials.

**Happy Feet** is a 2006 animated [jukebox musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jukebox_musical) [comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film) directed and produced by [George Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Miller_%28filmmaker%29) and written by Miller, [John Collee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Collee), [Judy Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Morris) and Warren Coleman. It stars [Elijah Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elijah_Wood), [Robin Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Williams), [Brittany Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittany_Murphy), [Hugh Jackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Jackman), [Nicole Kidman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Kidman), [Hugo Weaving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Weaving), [Anthony LaPaglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_LaPaglia), [Magda Szubanski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magda_Szubanski) and [Steve Irwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Irwin). In the film, Mumble (Wood), a tapdancing [emperor penguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_penguin) who lacks the ability to sing a heartsong to attract a soulmate and is ridiculed by his peers and family, departs on a journey across Antarctica to learn what is causing the local fish population to decline.

Happy Feet was the first animated film produced by [Kennedy Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Miller_Productions) and [Animal Logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Logic). An [international co-production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_co-production) between the United States and Australia, the film was produced at Sydney-based [visual effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_effects) and [animation studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animation_studio) [Animal Logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Logic). The film was released in North America on 17 November 2006 and in [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia) on 26 December. A planned IMAX 3D release was cancelled due to budgetary issues.<sup>[4]</sup>

Happy Feet received generally positive reviews from critics, with praise for its visuals, storyline and songs, and grossed \$384 million against its \$100 million budget, becoming the [tenth-highest-grossing film of 2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_in_film#Highest-grossing_films). It earned the inaugural [BAFTA Award for Best Animated Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Animated_Film), and the [Academy Award for Best Animated Feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature), and was nominated for the [Annie Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature) and the [Saturn Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Award_for_Best_Animated_Film) for Best Animated Feature.

Plot

Every [emperor penguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_penguin) attracts a [mate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mating) by singing a unique "heartsong". If the [male](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male) penguin's heartsong matches the [female](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female)'s song, the two penguins mate. Norma Jean, a female penguin, falls for Memphis, a male penguin and they become mates. They lay an egg, which Memphis cares for while Norma Jean leaves with the other females to [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing). While the males struggle through the harsh [winter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter), Memphis briefly drops the egg. The resulting chick, Mumble, is unable to sing but is nevertheless enamored with Gloria, a female penguin who is regarded as the most talented of her age. One day, Mumble discovers he is able to [tap dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tap_dance) before encountering a group of hostile [skua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skua), with a leader who is tagged with a [yellow band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_ringing), which he says is from an [alien abduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alien_abduction). Mumble narrowly escapes the hungry birds by falling into a crevice.

Now a young adult, Mumble is frequently ridiculed by the elders and their leader Noah. After escaping from a [leopard seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopard_seal) attack, Mumble befriends five [Adelie penguins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelie_penguin) named Ramón, Nestor, Lombardo, Rinaldo and Raul, known collectively as "the Amigos", who embrace Mumble's dance moves and assimilate him into their group. After seeing a hidden human [excavator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excavator) in an avalanche, they opt to ask Lovelace, a [rockhopper penguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_rockhopper_penguin), about its origin. For the emperor penguins, it is mating season and Gloria is the center of attention. The Amigos unsuccessfully attempt to help Mumble win her affection by having Ramón sing a Spanish version of "[My Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Way)" behind Mumble, with the latter [lip syncing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lip_sync). After Mumble desperately begins tap dancing in sync with her song, she falls for him and the youthful penguins join in for singing and dancing to "[Boogie Wonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boogie_Wonderland)". The elders are appalled by Mumble's conduct, which they see as the reason for their lean fishing season. Memphis begs Mumble to stop dancing, for his own sake, but when Mumble refuses, he is exiled.

Mumble and the Amigos return to Lovelace, only to find him being choked by the plastic rings. Lovelace confesses they were snagged on him while swimming off the forbidden shores, beyond the land of the

[elephant seals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elephant_seals). Not long into their journey, Gloria encounters them, wishing to become Mumble's mate. Fearing for her safety, he ridicules Gloria, driving her away.

At the forbidden shore, Mumble, Lovelace, and the Amigos are attacked by two [orcas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orca), during which Lovelace is freed from the plastic rings. After escaping, they find a fishing boat and climb atop a tall iceberg. In the distance, they see several more boats, the cause of their fish scarcity. Mumble jumps into the water and exhaustingly pursues them alone, eventually washing up on a beach. He is rescued and brought to Marine World, a fictional zoo in [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami), in an exhibit with [Magellanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magellanic_penguin) and [chinstrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinstrap_penguin) penguins. After a long and secluded confinement unsuccessfully attempting to communicate with humans visiting the exhibit, he is about to succumb to [madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insanity) when he unexpectedly reveals his dancing skills to the humans, who are all amazed. He is released back into the wild with a [tracking device](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPS_wildlife_tracking) attached to his back. He returns to his colony and challenges the will of the elders. Memphis reconciles with him just as a research team arrives, verifying Mumble's statements of "aliens" existing. The entire colony engages in dance in front of the research team, whose expedition footage prompts a worldwide debate which eventually results in a ban on all Antarctic [overfishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overfishing), satisfying both the emperor penguins and the Amigos.
